subject: Critical Thinking
title: Treating People as Ends, Not Means
description: A micro-lesson that makes Treating People as Ends, Not Means usable.

hook.text: You hire someone just to impress a client. You date someone just to make your ex jealous. You're using people as tools.

buildup.text: Kant's second formulation: 'Treat humanity, in yourself and others, always as an end and never merely as a means.'

discovery.text: People have inherent dignity – they're not instruments for your goals.

twist.text: 'Merely' is key: it's okay to use a taxi driver's services if you also respect them as a person.

climax.text: Slavery, exploitation, & manipulation all violate this: they reduce persons to tools.

punchline.text: People are not tools. They're not stepping stones. They're not means.

quiz.question: What does Kant mean by treating people as 'ends in themselves'?
options: Respecting their inherent dignity and autonomy, never using them merely as instruments

details.summary: Kant's second formulation of the categorical imperative insists that people must never be used merely as tools for someone else's goals. Every person has inherent dignity that demands respect regardless of utility.
details.whyItMatters: This principle forms the backbone of human rights and consent, shaping laws against exploitation and coercion worldwide.
takeaways: People have inherent worth beyond their usefulness
Using someone merely as a means violates their dignity
Consent transforms instrumental interactions into moral ones

faq.question: What does it mean to treat someone merely as a means?
faq.answer: It means exploiting them purely for your benefit without regard for their own goals, consent, or well-being—like deceiving someone to extract money from them.

faq.question: Can you ever use people as means without violating Kantian ethics?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as you also respect their autonomy. Hiring a plumber uses them as a means, but paying fairly and respecting their consent treats them as an end too.
